quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds have an incredible memory and can remember every flower they've visited and how long it will take each flower to refill with nectar. They can even remember which flowers they visited a year ago during their migration! This amazing spatial memory helps them efficiently gather the nectar they need for their high-energy lifestyle.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Hummingbirds in the Pacific Northwest
short_read.teaser: Anna's and Rufous hummingbirds are year-round neighbors in the Olympic Peninsula, with personalities as vibrant as their feathers. Learn why these tiny birds are tougher than they look and how they survive Pacific Northwest winters.

medium_read.title: The Hungarian Embroidery Tradition: Threads Through Time
medium_read.teaser: For centuries, Hungarian women have passed down intricate embroidery patterns that tell stories of villages, regions, and families. These beautiful textiles are more than decoration—they're a living connection to heritage and community.

long_read.title: The Return of Sea Otters to the Olympic Coast
long_read.teaser: Once hunted to near extinction, sea otters are slowly returning to Washington's coastal waters, bringing dramatic changes to kelp forests and marine ecosystems. Their story is one of resilience, conservation success, and the delicate balance of ocean life.

port_angeles.title: Butterfly Season at the Olympic Discovery Trail
port_angeles.description: Late summer is peak butterfly season along the Olympic Discovery Trail! Watch for painted ladies, admirals, and swallowtails dancing among the wildflowers. The section near Port Angeles Harbor is especially beautiful right now, with native plants attracting dozens of species.

puzzle_1.question: A ruby-throated hummingbird's heart beats about ___ times per minute while flying.
puzzle_1.correct_response: That's exactly right! It's hard to imagine such a tiny heart beating that fast, but hummingbirds are truly remarkable little creatures.
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's heart actually beats about 1,200 times per minute during flight—that's 20 times per second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: A hummingbird's heart beats an incredible 1,200 times per minute while flying! By comparison, our hearts beat only about 60-100 times per minute at rest.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To power their incredibly fast wing beats (up to 80 times per second), hummingbirds have the highest metabolism of any animal. They must eat every 10-15 minutes and consume up to half their body weight in nectar each day!

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful! Pillangó is indeed the Hungarian word for butterfly—such a lovely, flowing word for such a delicate creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó'—doesn't it sound beautiful? (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is part of the Finno-Ugric language family and is unrelated to the Germanic and Romance languages around it. Many Hungarian words have a melodic, flowing quality like pillangó.

puzzle_3.question: What do sea otters use to crack open shellfish while floating on their backs?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Yes! Sea otters are one of the few animals that use tools. They often keep a favorite rock in a pouch of loose skin under their forearm and use it like an anvil to crack open clams and sea urchins!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Sea otters actually use rocks or stones as tools! They balance them on their chests while floating and bang shellfish against them to crack them open. Some otters even have a favorite rock they keep with them!
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Sea otters are among the most intelligent marine mammals and are skilled tool users. They've been observed using rocks not just for food, but also to dislodge prey from crevices in kelp forests.
